extracted.intended_audience: systematic reviewers, epidemiologists, HTA researchers and authors of empirical studies on publication/time-lag bias
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction and assessment of empirical studies that evaluate time-lag/publication delay bias (i.e., whether statistically significant results are published faster). Includes extraction of study-level metrics (sample size, design, effect measures, p-values, CIs) and methodological/reporting quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time lag bias – included empirical studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Time lag bias – included empirical studies (Appendix 10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and extract empirical studies that examined time-lag/publication delay bias; capture how each study measured and reported time lag (e.g., time from study completion to publication, median delays, survival/time-to-event methods). Compare time-to-publication between groups (e.g., significant vs non-significant results).

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the reported result pertains to the study's primary outcome (page text repeatedly labels results as 'primary').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record if the analysed/resulting metric is the pre-specified primary outcome vs a secondary/other outcome; many analyses compare publication delays for primary outcomes specifically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical significance (significant vs non-significant)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification of results by statistical significance (text includes phrases like 'significance - non' and p thresholds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify study findings as statistically significant (commonly p<0.05) or non-significant and compare publication timing between these groups; report p-values and how significance was defined/categorised in each empirical study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect size and 95% confidence interval
rubrics_metrics.description: Effect estimates are reported with 95% confidence intervals (many entries show values with '95% CI').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extract the reported effect measure (e.g., RR, OR, hazard ratio, rate ratio) and its 95% CI; use these to quantify association between significance (or favourable results) and time-to-publication and to assess precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: p-values and significance thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Use and reporting of p-values and explicit thresholds (e.g., p<0.05, p reported as ranges or exact values).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extract exact p-values or category (e.g., p<0.05, p between ranges) used by each study; note any multiple-testing adjustments or thresholds different from conventional 0.05.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size (n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Study/sample size reporting (the page lists n and numbers of studies/participants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record sample sizes (number of studies, number of trials, number of participants) used in analyses; consider sample size in interpretation and in weighting meta-analytic estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study design classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Designation of study design types (randomized controlled trials, observational/cohort, surveys, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extract study design (RCT, cohort, case–control, survey of investigators, etc.) and, where applicable, stratify or subgroup analyses by design type to see if time-lag effects differ by design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-to-publication / publication delay metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Metrics for publication delay such as median time to publication, interquartile range, hazard/ rate ratios comparing groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extract reported metrics of publication delay (median/IQR, mean, hazard ratios, rate ratios), methods used (e.g., survival analysis), and statistical comparisons between groups (significant vs non-significant, favourable vs unfavourable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Direction of effect / whether results favour intervention
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether reported results 'favour' the intervention (text includes 'favour'/'favouring' terms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record if study outcomes favour the experimental intervention or treatment and examine whether 'favourable' findings are associated with faster publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selective outcome reporting / reporting bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Selective reporting or discrepancies between what was planned and what was reported (the appendix addresses reporting/selective reporting issues).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess evidence of selective outcome reporting (e.g., differences between protocol and published report, missing outcomes) and consider this as a dimension related to publication/timeliness bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response rates (for surveys/interviews)
rubrics_metrics.description: Response rates of investigators or journals when surveys were used (page shows response-related entries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When empirical studies used surveys to collect data about publication, extract response rates and consider non-response bias when interpreting findings on publication delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion / exclusion criteria for empirical studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria used to include or exclude empirical studies in the review (the appendix enumerates included studies and selection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the inclusion/exclusion rules each empirical study applied (time periods, types of outcomes, definitions of completion/publication) because these affect comparability and potential bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological / reporting quality of included studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of methodological quality and reporting completeness of the empirical studies (mentions 'reporting quality', 'method' details).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extract any quality assessments (risk-of-bias domains, reporting completeness, verification of dates) performed by the empirical study and use these to judge reliability of their time-lag estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stratified / subgroup analyses and heterogeneity
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of subgroup or stratified analyses (by outcome type, study design, sample size, etc.) and heterogeneity reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture whether empirical studies performed subgroup analyses (e.g., by primary vs secondary outcomes, trial phase, design) and any heterogeneity or interaction findings relevant to time-lag effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods for association between result characteristics and publication timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical approaches used to link result characteristics (significance, direction, outcome type) with publication timing (mentions RR, CI, p-values, survival methods).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extract which statistical models/methods (e.g., Cox proportional hazards, rate ratios, logistic regression) each empirical study used to test the association between study/result characteristics and time-to-publication, and note modelling covariates and adjustments.
